h1: API 570 Training: Self-Paced Exam Preparation for the Piping Inspector Certification
html:
API 570 training for the piping inspector examination

API 570 certification is the credential refineries, chemical plants and inspection contractors look for in the people who plan and carry out in-service inspection of process piping. The examination is set by the American Petroleum Institute, which also decides each candidate's eligibility and issues the certificate. You sit it in person at a Prometric centre: 170 questions over a 7.5-hour day, 110 closed-book in 2.75 hours and 60 open-book in 3.75 hours after a 45-minute lunch, with 140 of the 170 counting toward your result.

The Atlantis NDT API 570 course prepares you for that examination. You study online at your own pace, from the day you enrol to the window you book, and an instructor answers your questions as you meet them. The application, the eligibility decision, the exam and the certificate all stay with API.

Who takes API 570, and the eligibility rules in brief

The typical candidate has spent years around piping already: an ultrasonic thickness technician who has logged readings at thousands of condition monitoring locations, a welder who moved into QA/QC, an operator who joined the inspection department, or a reliability engineer who approves piping inspection plans. Many add API 570 to API 510 or API 653, because owner-users like one inspector who can cover the vessels, tanks and the piping between them.

API decides eligibility on education plus in-service metallic piping experience gained within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract to, an authorized inspection agency. An engineering or technology degree needs one year supervising or performing inspection. A two-year degree or certificate calls for two years of piping experience, a high school diploma three, and no formal education five or more, each with at least one year in inspection. The API 570 certification requirements page has the detail, including how military service counts.

What is on the API 570 exam: the publications and their editions

Each set of API 570 windows has its own Body of Knowledge and Publications Effectivity Sheet. When this page was written, the sheet API had published for its upcoming API 570 windows listed the editions below. Download the sheet for the window you book, because editions change and the exam follows the sheet.

PublicationEdition on the sheetScope examined
API 5705th edition, 2024Entire code
API RP 5713rd edition, 2020Definitions and 15 listed damage mechanisms
API RP 5745th edition, 2024, with Addendum 1 (2025)Entire document
API RP 5765th edition, 2024Sections 5, 6.1 to 6.5 and 7
API RP 5773rd edition, 2020Entire document
API RP 5784th edition, 2023Entire document
ASME B31.32024 editionAll except 30 listed exclusions
ASME B16.52020 editionRatings, materials, dimensions, marking and testing
ASME Section V2023 editionArticles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10, and SE-797 in Article 23
ASME Section IX2023 editionWelding only
ASME PCC-22022 editionTwelve listed repair and testing articles

The B31.3 exclusions matter as much as the inclusions. Branch reinforcement, the other pressure-design paragraphs beyond straight pipe and blanks, flexibility analysis, Category M and high pressure piping are outside the Body of Knowledge, so the course spends your B31.3 time on quality factors, pressure design, materials and impact testing, fabrication, heat treatment, examination and leak testing. The RP 571 mechanisms are the ones piping inspectors meet most, from corrosion under insulation and sour water corrosion to vibration fatigue, soil corrosion and sulfidation. See the ASME B31.3 explainer and the API 570 code explainer for background.

API 570 calculations, worked through

The Body of Knowledge lists the calculations precisely: corrosion rate, remaining life and interval; casting and weld joint quality factors; pressure design and blank thickness; the MAWP of corroded pipe; test pressure; impact testing; preheat and heat treatment; thermal expansion; and flange ratings. These examples use round numbers that carry from one to the next.

Pressure design thickness of straight pipe (B31.3, 304.1.2)

NPS 6 pipe has an outside diameter D of 6.625 in. Take P = 600 psi, an allowable stress S of 20,000 psi given in the problem, E = 1.0 for seamless pipe, W = 1.0, and Y = 0.4 from Table 304.1.1 for ferritic steels up to 900°F. Then t = PD ÷ 2(SEW + PY) = 3,975 ÷ 40,480 = 0.098 in., and the minimum required thickness tm adds the allowance c. In service, readings are judged against the greater of that and a structural minimum, because thin small-bore pipe can satisfy pressure long after it stops carrying its own weight; RP 574 discusses structural minimums. Swap to electric-resistance-welded pipe and E falls to 0.85 from Table A-1B, a common source of wrong answers.

Corrosion rate, remaining life and the interval by piping class

At one condition monitoring location (CML) the baseline reading was 0.275 in. 12 years ago, the previous one 0.230 in. four years ago, and today's is 0.205 in. The owner's structural minimum of 0.110 in. exceeds the pressure design thickness, so it governs.

  • Long-term rate = (0.275 − 0.205) ÷ 12 = 0.0058 in. per year; short-term rate = (0.230 − 0.205) ÷ 4 = 0.00625 in. per year, the higher.
  • Remaining life = (0.205 − 0.110) ÷ 0.00625 = 15.2 years.
  • Thickness interval = the lesser of half the remaining life (7.6 years) and the class maximum in API 570 Table 1: 7.6 years for Class 2 or Class 3, whose maximum is 10 years, but 5 years for Class 1.

External visual inspection has its own maximums, 5 years for Classes 1 and 2 and 10 for Class 3, while Class 4 intervals are left to the owner-user. Questions often hide the class inside a description of the fluid. See the guides to piping service classes and long-term and short-term corrosion rates.

MAWP of corroded pipe (API 570, 7.5)

API 570 subtracts twice the corrosion expected before the next inspection from the measured thickness, then uses B31.3 rearranged for pressure: P = 2SEWt ÷ (D − 2Yt). With 0.205 in., 0.00625 in. per year and the next inspection in 5 years, the thickness used is 0.205 − 2 × 0.03125 = 0.1425 in., and P = 5,700 ÷ 6.511 = about 875 psi. The pipe wall is not the limit at 600 psi, so check the flanges and valves next.

Flange rating and the most economical flange (B16.5)

Find the material group in Table 1.1-1 (forged A105 is Group 1.1), then read that group's rating table. In the 2020 edition, Group 1.1 is rated 285 psig for Class 150 and 740 psig for Class 300 from −20°F to 100°F, so a line at 600 psig and 100°F needs Class 300. Ratings fall as temperature rises, interpolation between table temperatures is allowed, and a hotter line can push you up a class.

Leak test pressure (B31.3, 345)

Hydrostatic test pressure is PT = 1.5 × P × Rr, where Rr is allowable stress at test temperature over that at design temperature, capped at 6.5. With 20,000 psi at test and 18,000 psi at a hot design temperature, Rr = 1.111 and PT = 1.5 × 600 × 1.111 = about 1,000 psi. A pneumatic test is 1.1 times design pressure, 660 psi here, with extra safeguards for stored energy. The pressure is held at least 10 minutes before the leak examination, and B31.3 lets a hydrotest pressure that would exceed yield be reduced.

Impact testing, blanks, preheat and expansion

Figure 323.2.2A gives the lowest temperature a carbon steel may see without impact testing at its thickness, and Table 323.3.5 the Charpy values tests must reach. Blank thickness under 304.5.3 is worked from the gasket's inside diameter (or the ring-joint pitch diameter), not the pipe's. Preheat comes from Table 330.1.1 and heat treatment from paragraph 331. Table C-1 gives expansion in inches per 100 ft from 70°F: at 1.8 in. per 100 ft, a 250 ft run grows 4.5 in.

Beyond the numbers: CMLs, circuits and inspection planning

Many API 570 questions test whether you can plan inspection the way the code intends, with RP 574 as the explanation:

  • Circuits and CMLs: group piping of similar material and service, put more CMLs where corrosion is localised or a leak would matter most, and read the same spot each time so the rates mean something.
  • Injection and mix points: circuits in their own right (injection point inspection).
  • Deadlegs: stagnant branches that can corrode far faster than the active line (deadleg inspection).
  • Corrosion under insulation: the temperatures and locations most at risk (CUI in inspection plans).
  • Soil-to-air interfaces, small-bore and buried piping, repairs and rerating: each with its own expectations, including what needs the inspector's authorisation.

Welding, PWHT and NDE questions on the API 570 exam

Section IX questions hand you a WPS and PQR, or a welder's record, and ask whether they comply, limited to one process per document (SMAW, GTAW, GMAW or SAW) and P-No. 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8 base metals. RP 577 is examined in full, and B31.3 adds preheat, heat treatment and the extent of examination. If procedure qualification is new to you, read the guide to WPS, PQR and WPQ early. The API 570 list of Section V articles is wider than the API 510 list, adding visual examination (Article 9) and leak testing (Article 10); expect questions on what a compliant procedure contains rather than on interpreting indications.

Is the API 570 exam open book? Working the B31.3 PDF

Only the last 60 questions are open-book, on PDFs the test centre provides, so nothing you have marked up comes in with you. B31.3 is long and open-book questions often come from its tables: A-1 allowable stresses, A-1B quality factors, 323.3.5 impact values, 330.1.1 preheat and the B16.5 ratings. Know the table numbers so you can go straight to them, read the notes under each table, and flag any question that is eating your time. The closed-book half needs the formulas, class intervals, definitions and RP 574 practice from memory, and the course's timed papers copy both halves.

How to pass the API 570 exam: a study sequence

  1. Get the documents for your window, in the editions the sheet names.
  2. Read API 570 cover to cover; it carries most closed-book marks.
  3. Read RP 574 alongside it as the explanation of the code.
  4. Master the calculation set until every formula is automatic.
  5. Learn B31.3 navigation, including what is excluded.
  6. Cover damage mechanisms and welding: RP 571, RP 577, Section IX and PCC-2.
  7. Sit full timed papers, tracing each wrong answer to its paragraph.

No fixed time applies; it depends on how much you already use at work. The sign you are ready is steady scores on full timed papers. Free questions to use with the course are on the API 570 practice questions page.

API 570 online exam prep: what to look for in a course

You will find intensive seminars before each window, blended programmes, recorded lessons and big question banks. A piping inspector on a rotating schedule usually gets more from material they can return to than from a block they must attend. Check that the course names your sheet's editions, teaches the B31.3 and API 570 calculations step by step, lets you ask a person and copies the real exam split. Treat banks advertised as real exam questions with care: answers taken from an older B31.3 or API 570 can be wrong for your window. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider; the course is independent preparation.

Sponsoring API 570 candidates, and what comes after the exam

Contractors and owner-users often enrol several piping inspectors together to meet a contract that names API 570 inspectors or to build cover before a turnaround, and each moves at the speed their background allows. Each must still meet API's rules and apply individually. Fees are quoted on request.

The API 570 Piping Inspector certification runs for three years. Recertifying takes at least 20% of your last three years on piping inspection, 24 hours of continuing professional development in at least two categories and, every six years, a 25-question open-book web quiz; miss the 90-day grace period and you start again with the full exam. Atlantis also runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based UT Level II training, AWS CWI exam prep and remote risk-based inspection studies for owners setting piping intervals by risk.

faq.q: Is the API 570 exam open book?
faq.a: Only partly. Of the 170 questions, 110 are closed-book and answered from memory in 2.75 hours. The other 60 are open-book: the examined publications, including B31.3 and B16.5, are on screen as PDFs for 3.75 hours. You cannot take your own copies or tabs into the Prometric centre, so practise finding tables in plain PDFs.

faq.q: What calculations are on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Corrosion rate, remaining life and interval by piping class from API 570; casting and weld joint quality factors, straight-pipe pressure design thickness and blank thickness from B31.3; MAWP of corroded pipe; hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure; impact-test exemption and Charpy values; preheat and heat treatment; thermal expansion; and flange ratings and class selection from B16.5. Branch reinforcement is excluded.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 online?
faq.a: Yes. The Atlantis course is self-paced and online: you begin when you enrol, fit study around your shifts, and an instructor answers questions on calculations and code paragraphs. The examination is a separate step: you apply to API, which holds it in person at Prometric test centres in set windows (see API exam windows).

faq.q: Which B31.3 edition is on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: The one on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for your window. When this page was written, the sheet API had published for its upcoming API 570 windows listed B31.3 2024 with API 570 5th edition and B16.5 2020. Editions change between windows, so download the sheet for the window you book and study those editions.

faq.q: Should I take API 510 or API 570 first?
faq.a: It depends on your equipment and what your employer or clients ask for. Piping is a large share of the inspection workload at most refineries and chemical plants, so many start with API 570; others start with API 510 because they mainly inspect vessels. The two share several references, which shortens the second; see which API certification to take first.

faq.q: Do I have to be an NDT technician to take API 570?
faq.a: No. API looks at education and in-service piping experience from the last 10 years with an authorized inspection agency, including at least a year supervising or performing inspection. NDT technicians are common candidates, but welders, operators and engineers qualify the same way, and no NDT certification is required; see the API 570 certification page.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis API 570 course approved by API?
faq.a: No. Atlantis NDT is not an API-approved, API-accredited or API-endorsed training provider. The course is independent exam preparation built on the Body of Knowledge and effectivity sheet API publishes. API decides eligibility, administers the examination and issues the API 570 certification; completing any course, including ours, does not certify you.
